programmes.label: Middle Eastern Studies at University of Groningen

exception.reason: UCR offers related study of empires, Mediterranean exchange, literature and international relations. Even when combined in a feasible programme, these courses do not provide sustained study of modern Middle Eastern societies, politics and religious traditions or the regional methods needed to connect those subjects. These are central to Groningen’s degree.
exception.curriculumContext: Verified 18-component regular Middle Eastern Studies BA for September 2026, 180 EC.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Screened all workbook identities and read the substantive contributions of both feasible trial schedules. History of Empires includes ancient Persia. Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean covers connections with Islamic courts. World Myth & Literature includes Arabic and Near Eastern material. Peace & Conflict, comparative politics, international law and media contribute complementary methods and wider context. Their actual content does not establish sustained modern Middle Eastern study. The conclusion is based on programme substance, independently of offering conflicts, Arabic language and study abroad.

candidateAssessment.concept: Comparative History, Conflict and Middle East–Europe Relations
candidateAssessment.assessment: The strongest trial combines empire, Mediterranean connections, Arabic and Near Eastern narratives, conflict, EU politics and international relations. Ancient Persia and Renaissance Mediterranean exchange contribute real regional content, but the plan does not sustain modern Middle Eastern history, politics or region-specific methods. General conflict and international relations cannot supply the missing regional inquiry.

The strongest cultural materials are Eastern Mediterranean artistic exchange and Arabic literary examples. Media, life writing and sociology support comparative interpretation but do not establish sustained study of modern Middle Eastern societies, migration and soft power.

Arabic narratives appear in translation and do not establish a regional source-based course sequence. This candidate lacks a sustained area-studies focus independently of the absence of language acquisition or a study-abroad placement.

candidateAssessment.concept: Religion and Diversity in the Middle East
candidateAssessment.assessment: Islamic courts and Arabic narratives contribute cultural examples. The workbook does not establish sustained study of Judaism and Islam as traditions or of their relationships with political life and social diversity in the region.

audience.programmeDescription: Middle Eastern Studies at the University of Groningen is taught in Dutch and examines the region’s history, politics, cultures and religious traditions. Students learn Arabic, complete a minor and write a thesis. The standard second-year curriculum includes a semester in Cairo or Rabat.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR courses explore empires, Mediterranean art and literature alongside comparative politics and international relations. Groningen offers sustained study of modern Middle Eastern societies, regional politics and religious traditions. The table shows Groningen’s curriculum.
